notes:
Stage: procurement but deal effectively frozen. CTO + VP Eng very pragmatic. Primary objection is unit economics on our suggested setup:
- Dense rerank workload with 30k tokens/context on 100k queries/mo -> token spend projections 3x initial budget.
- Dedicated GPU commit to hit latency targets required a 3-month reserved pool; procurement says commit size unacceptable vs burst/GPU spot options.
- They ran a quick cost delta vs NimbusAI and an open self-hosted stack: "we can't justify 3x TCO for similar latency" (quote from Raj Patel, CTO).
Security: SOC2 + KMS ok but they require per-request retention guarantees and granular audit logs; legal asked for a custom SLAs addendum.
Champion: Sara Kim (Prod Mgmt) led POC but left in Nov for a competitor; internal momentum dissipated.
POC notes: ran embeddings + rerank on 7k docs; quality looked good, but throughput needs (burst vs sustained) changed cost model badly.
Sales tact: proposed Optimize plan + aggressive batching + quantized model variants to drop cost 30-40% — team pushed back that savings are theoretical for their worst-case query mix.
Outcome: last week procurement paused approval pending a new internal cost model. Re-engagement attempts (emails, call invite) unresponsive.
Suggested follow-ups: hand off to channel partner pricing team? Or propose a limited committed burst with strict budget cap to test economics.

summary: Auric Bridge Systems ran a short POC for dense reranking + embeddings. Model quality and latency met targets on Dedicated hardware, but projected token and GPU commit costs created a persistent unit-economics gap against their budget and competitor quotes. Compound issues: lost internal champion, stringent retention/residency security asks, and procurement unwilling to accept our recommended commit size. Deal is currently stalled / effectively closed-lost to competitors or cost-constrained procurement.
